approach.method_basis: The Parent evolves scored molecular graphs through score-band parent selection, connected-fragment crossover and local mutation. Stable canonical admission creates a surplus pool. A Gaussian process learns from every earlier accepted raw score using folded counts of radius-two molecular environments and generalized Tanimoto similarity. It chooses evaluations through correlated posterior draws, then updates the archive, breeding population and incumbent using real raw scores.
approach.novelty: Add a fixed topological atom-pair count channel alongside the retained local counts, and average their separately normalized similarity kernels equally. Atom types separated by graph distances up to thirty bonds can provide relational information missing from local environment counts. Earlier unfolding kept the same local environments, while ordinal targets changed label spacing; both lost mean endpoint score. This tests additional molecular information through one fixed covariance composition, with raw-score targets and the search rules retained. Added information may also dilute useful locality, so alias splitting or better prediction alone will not establish benefit.

hypothesis: Retain the Parent's local Morgan occurrence-count covariance and add sparse topological atom-pair occurrence-count covariance, using the fixed equal-weight average of their separate generalized Tanimoto kernels for every GP block while preserving raw-score learning and the inherited search rules.

finding_summary.headline: Atom-pair information changed search and split six local aliases, but the mean endpoint fell by 0.033408
finding_summary.insights: More descriptor distinctions and better predictions on selected molecules did not yield better endpoint search in this fixed mixture. On the actual accepted stream, raw MSE improved from 0.009475 for the passive local model to 0.009335, and mean batch ordering correlation rose from 0.545819 to 0.571243, despite the endpoint loss. These improvements were uneven: MSE worsened in seven task/seed cells, including all median_2 cells. Ordinary similarity and regularization changes were broadly exposed, whereas alias-mediated benefit was not: ten members of five split pool pairs remained unscored, and only one member of the cross pair was evaluated. Thirteen other pairs shared atom-pair counts but remained distinguishable through local counts; the channels still do not establish complete molecular identity. The negative result belongs to this one equal-weight composition and does not undo the earlier evidence for retaining local occurrence counts or isolate atom-pair information from mixture weighting. Molecular evidence still shows reactive heteroatom-halogen and sulfur motifs, large linked assemblies and destructive fragments alongside conventional high-scoring chemistry. Added topological information does not enforce chemical feasibility, and neither a universal size explanation nor an alias-resolution explanation is established.
finding_summary.results: All 435 batches changed their raw posterior means, uncertainties and conditional covariance. Against the same-input local-only reference, 432 selected sets and 433 orders changed; three sets and two orders remained unchanged. All six distinct local-count alias pairs split, but none had both members scored. All three matched replicas completed. Mean final score fell from 0.595670 to 0.562261, a loss of 0.033408 against the required gain of 0.002. Seed deltas were −0.072325, +0.009185 and −0.037084. Six of fifteen task/seed endpoints improved: all three zaleplon results and the seed-1 deco_hop, drd2 and sitagliptin results. Every median_2 result declined. Seed dispersion decreased from 0.026593 to 0.006995 around the lower mean. The mechanism ran correctly; its registered endpoint-benefit prediction was falsified.

molecular.headline: Aromatic amides, aza heterocycles and aryl amines persist; reactive bonds and unresolved ring geometry remain
molecular.overall_character: All fifteen Child and fifteen published Parent trajectory files were read: Search Seeds 0, 1 and 2, 300 observations per task/seed, with 900 records and 870 optimizer proposals per task. No task or Parent path is missing. The fresh brief marks both Child completion and matched Parent pairing complete, with no profile mismatches; the comparison is to n-62daf219c70a. The evaluated output contains compact fused aromatic carboxamides, linked nitrogen-rich carbonyl/thione heterocycles, polycyclic aryl amines, aromatic lactam/urea assemblies and fluorinated unsaturated nitrogen-carbonyl rings. Ring-closure text incidence is 0.9529 to 0.9805 and aromatic-text incidence 0.9276 to 0.977. These are molecule-level text incidences, not ring counts or aromatic-atom fractions. All stereocentre-text rates are zero. Charge-text incidence is zero except for one charge-separated nitrogen motif in the aromatic-amide task, rate 0.0011; neutral representations still contain basic amines. The chemical reading is rich rings/aromaticity, questionable synthetic plausibility, weak overall drug-likeness and moderate structural diversity across seeds, with narrower families among leaders within a seed. Conventional functional groups coexist with N-halogen and O-F bonds, unusual sulfur-H oxo environments and difficult bridges. No synthesis, stability, protonation, conformation or biological activity has been established. Sizes below are heavy-atom-token counts from the actual SMILES, not geometric measurements. The trajectory/offspring audit joins all 4,350 accepted offspring to their raw score, actual selected pool position and earlier evaluated parents. All fifteen raw-score leaders were evaluated and immediately admitted as survivors, and their scores agree with final best_so_far records. Immediate admission does not establish that every other evaluated molecule survives later replacement. The digest's final excerpt is a late seed-2 proposal list, not the retained leader of each seed. Full pool logs, rather than evaluated-only trajectories, support the pool observations below. Logged descriptors preserve the distinction between retained folded local Morgan counts and the added native sparse atom-pair counts. The receipts specify chirality-aware two-dimensional distances 1 through 30 and a fixed equal average of separately normalized count-Tanimoto kernels. Six distinct local-count-equal pairs occur in core training/cross/pool operands: five within-pool pairs and one archive-to-pool pair seen twice, hence seven occurrences; training contributes none. All six have unequal atom-pair rows and mixed similarity below one. Five additional pool_equivalence records repeat the five pool pairs and are not new pairs or independent observations. No distinct pair remains equal in both channels in these logged operands. This absence is conditional on the actual panel, not proof of molecular uniqueness. None of the ten members of the five within-pool pairs was evaluated in its task/seed. The cross pair has only one evaluated member: the 80-heavy-atom nitrogen-dione assembly in seed 2/evaluation 239 of the linked-heterocycle task, score 0.5910185045885361, immediately admitted but not an incumbent improvement. Its other member has no raw label. The six splits therefore supply no paired scored comparison. Conversely, thirteen distinct pairs remain equal in the atom-pair component alone while local counts distinguish them. Ten involve different single atoms with empty atom-pair rows; three involve sulfur-H or ring-bond variants. Their mixed similarities are below one, so component equality must not be called mixed-kernel equality. Finite identifiers, equal descriptor multisets, unspecified stereochemistry and restricted two-dimensional distances still limit identity and feasibility claims. The 435 passive local-only records explicitly have no alternative labels. Their predictions and choices are not another scored search, and a component or mixed similarity change does not demonstrate chemical benefit or mediation. Active posterior means are reported in raw-score units, covariance/noise in standardized raw-score units; the accepted labels and endpoint scores used here remain raw. Nothing here establishes global calibration. Historical applicability is retained as stated in the immutable brief: unfolding's nine unique aliases use joint training/cross/pool scope, whereas its seven within-pool occurrences are a narrower count; ordinal's six published pool pairs differ from the wider nine unique pairs across 51 joint occurrences. Their source-only atom-pair splits are conditional opportunity evidence, not current Child frequency, extra oracle outcomes or independent efficacy. Historical count-removal contrary gains, unfolding and ordinal endpoint exceptions, and the separate single-seed degree-pair source do not transfer or add their effects to this panel. The chemical associations below make no activation, eligibility, component-contribution or causal-mediation verdict. Reproducible trajectory, component-alias and provenance audits are under runs/SPIRAL2/.slots/r0019-00-improve-L01/molecular/.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.

        - atomInvariantsGenerator: atom invariants to be used during fingerprint generation

        - atomToBits: which bits each atom is involved in

finding_summary.headline: Atom-pair information changed search and split six local aliases, but the mean endpoint fell by 0.033408
finding_summary.insights: More descriptor distinctions and better predictions on selected molecules did not yield better endpoint search in this fixed mixture. On the actual accepted stream, raw MSE improved from 0.009475 for the passive local model to 0.009335, and mean batch ordering correlation rose from 0.545819 to 0.571243, despite the endpoint loss. These improvements were uneven: MSE worsened in seven task/seed cells, including all median_2 cells. Ordinary similarity and regularization changes were broadly exposed, whereas alias-mediated benefit was not: ten members of five split pool pairs remained unscored, and only one member of the cross pair was evaluated. Thirteen other pairs shared atom-pair counts but remained distinguishable through local counts; the channels still do not establish complete molecular identity. The negative result belongs to this one equal-weight composition and does not undo the earlier evidence for retaining local occurrence counts or isolate atom-pair information from mixture weighting. Molecular evidence still shows reactive heteroatom-halogen and sulfur motifs, large linked assemblies and destructive fragments alongside conventional high-scoring chemistry. Added topological information does not enforce chemical feasibility, and neither a universal size explanation nor an alias-resolution explanation is established.
finding_summary.results: All 435 batches changed their raw posterior means, uncertainties and conditional covariance. Against the same-input local-only reference, 432 selected sets and 433 orders changed; three sets and two orders remained unchanged. All six distinct local-count alias pairs split, but none had both members scored. All three matched replicas completed. Mean final score fell from 0.595670 to 0.562261, a loss of 0.033408 against the required gain of 0.002. Seed deltas were −0.072325, +0.009185 and −0.037084. Six of fifteen task/seed endpoints improved: all three zaleplon results and the seed-1 deco_hop, drd2 and sitagliptin results. Every median_2 result declined. Seed dispersion decreased from 0.026593 to 0.006995 around the lower mean. The mechanism ran correctly; its registered endpoint-benefit prediction was falsified.

    Get an atom pair fingerprint generator
    
      ARGUMENTS:
        - minDistance: minimum distance between atoms to be considered in a pair, default is 1 bond
        - maxDistance: maximum distance between atoms to be considered in a pair, default is maxPathLen-1 bonds
        - includeChirality: if set, chirality will be used in the atom  invariants, this is ignored if atomInvariantsGenerator is provided
        - use2D: if set, the 2D (topological) distance matrix  will be used
        - countSimulation:  if set, use count simulation while  generating the fingerprint

        - fpSize: size of the generated fingerprint, does not affect the sparse versions
        - atomInvariantsGenerator: atom invariants to be used during fingerprint generation
    
    This generator supports the following AdditionalOutput types:
        - atomToBits: which bits each atom is involved in
        - atomCounts: how many bits each atom sets
        - bitInfoMap: map from bitId to (atomId, radius) pairs

finding_summary.headline: Atom-pair information changed search and split six local aliases, but the mean endpoint fell by 0.033408
finding_summary.insights: More descriptor distinctions and better predictions on selected molecules did not yield better endpoint search in this fixed mixture. On the actual accepted stream, raw MSE improved from 0.009475 for the passive local model to 0.009335, and mean batch ordering correlation rose from 0.545819 to 0.571243, despite the endpoint loss. Ordinary similarity and regularization changes were broadly exposed, whereas alias-mediated benefit was not: ten members of five split pool pairs remained unscored, and only one member of the cross pair was evaluated. Thirteen other pairs shared atom-pair counts but remained distinguishable through local counts; the channels still do not establish complete molecular identity. The negative result belongs to this one equal-weight composition and does not undo the earlier evidence for retaining local occurrence counts or isolate atom-pair information from mixture weighting. Molecular evidence still shows reactive heteroatom-halogen and sulfur motifs, large linked assemblies and destructive fragments alongside conventional high-scoring chemistry.
